nodes.label: Maintenance list
nodes.detail: Renders $root.maintenanceList ordered by status (under maintenance > scheduled > inactive > ended). No rows means No Maintenance. The status is the row colour

nodes.label: Schedule maintenance button
nodes.detail: A link to /add-maintenance. It opens the create screen

nodes.label: Pause button
nodes.detail: Only on rows where item.active is true. Pressing it opens the confirm dialog and stashes the ID in selectedMaintenanceID

nodes.label: Resume button
nodes.detail: Only on rows where item.active is false. It sends resumeMaintenance immediately, with no confirm dialog

nodes.label: Clone button
nodes.detail: Navigates to /maintenance/clone/:id. After loading it clears the id and adds cloneOf to the title, so saving creates a new one

nodes.label: Edit button
nodes.detail: Navigates to /maintenance/edit/:id and opens the edit screen

nodes.label: Delete button
nodes.detail: Opens the confirm dialog and stashes the ID in selectedMaintenanceID

nodes.label: Pause confirm dialog
nodes.detail: "Yes" runs pauseMaintenance. No sends nothing

nodes.label: Delete confirm dialog
nodes.detail: "Yes" runs deleteMaintenance. It cannot be undone

nodes.label: Strategy picker
nodes.detail: Six choices: manual, single window, cron expression, or recurring (interval, weekday, day of month). The choice swaps the fields below it and which of them are required

nodes.label: Affected monitors (multi-select)
nodes.detail: A pseudo-entry, "Select All", sits at the top. Paused monitors are listed last

nodes.label: Show on all status pages
nodes.detail: Ticking it hides the individual picker and sends every candidate page at save time. Pages added later are not picked up automatically

nodes.label: Status pages (multi-select)
nodes.detail: Chooses which status pages announce it. It can be saved with none selected as long as there is at least one monitor

nodes.label: Quick duration buttons
nodes.detail: Only for a single window. It fills the end time from the start time plus the given minutes. With no start time it just shows an error toast

nodes.label: Save button
nodes.detail: Disabled while processing. submit only runs after the form's required checks pass

nodes.label: No-monitors confirmation
nodes.detail: Appears only when there are zero monitors but at least one status page. Yes continues the save

nodes.label: Error toast
nodes.detail: Shows, verbatim, the messages for empty monitors and pages, a failed request, or a server-side exception

nodes.label: Window display
nodes.detail: "Manual" for manual; otherwise the head of timeslotList (the current or next window) shown as a time range with its UTC offset

nodes.label: Edit screen init
nodes.detail: For a new one it builds the defaults (single window, one hour from now). For an edit or a clone it calls getMaintenance and then fetches the two kinds of targets

nodes.label: Toggle select-all
nodes.detail: Runs only when "Select All" is chosen. If everything is already selected it empties the list, otherwise it puts every candidate back in

nodes.label: Work out and fill the end time
nodes.detail: With no start time it shows a toast and stops. Otherwise it writes start + minutes into the end field as a local-time string

nodes.label: Save entry point
nodes.detail: With zero monitors but at least one status page it opens the confirm dialog and waits. Otherwise it goes straight to doSubmit

nodes.label: The save itself
nodes.detail: Both empty aborts with an error. New and clone send addMaintenance, an edit sends editMaintenance, and after success the two kinds of targets are registered in turn

nodes.label: Send the affected monitors
nodes.detail: Sends the selected monitor array as is. A failure only toasts and it moves on to the next step

nodes.label: Send the target pages
nodes.detail: With "all pages" it sends every candidate, otherwise the selection. A failure only toasts and the navigation still happens

nodes.label: Sort the list
nodes.detail: Descending by status weight (under maintenance 1000 down to unknown 0), then by title. It is recomputed every time maintenanceList arrives

nodes.label: Send the pause
nodes.detail: Emits pauseMaintenance with the stashed selectedMaintenanceID and toasts the result

nodes.label: Send the resume
nodes.detail: Takes the row's ID as an argument and emits resumeMaintenance. No confirmation in between

nodes.label: Send the delete
nodes.detail: Emits deleteMaintenance with selectedMaintenanceID. On success it stays on /maintenance

nodes.label: Emit addMaintenance
nodes.detail: A thin wrapper that sends the maintenance form content over socket.io

nodes.label: Emit the affected monitors
nodes.detail: A thin wrapper that sends the maintenance ID and the monitor array on addMonitorMaintenance

nodes.label: Emit the announcement pages
nodes.detail: A thin wrapper that sends the maintenance ID and the page array on addMaintenanceStatusPage

nodes.label: Emit getMaintenanceList
nodes.detail: Asks for the list again. With no callback it passes an empty function

nodes.label: Emit deleteMaintenance
nodes.detail: A thin wrapper that sends the maintenance ID

nodes.label: Receive the list
nodes.detail: Replaces maintenanceList from the server wholesale. It updates on its own from actions on other screens, without anyone pressing anything here

nodes.label: socket.io connection accepted
nodes.detail: socket.io connection accepted. Every UI-initiated action passes through here

nodes.label: addMaintenance received
nodes.detail: Check login, turn the form into a bean, save it, put it in the in-memory list and call run(true). A failure comes back as ok:false with a message

nodes.label: editMaintenance received
nodes.detail: Takes the bean from memory and answers Permission denied to anyone but its creator. Overwrites it and re-arms with run(true)

nodes.label: addMonitorMaintenance received
nodes.detail: Deletes every monitor link and puts back what it was sent. There is no owner check, only a login check

nodes.label: addMaintenanceStatusPage received
nodes.detail: Deletes every status page link, puts back what it was sent, and drops the public page cache

nodes.label: getMaintenance received
nodes.detail: Reads the one row where id and user_id match. Someone else's ID leaves bean null, toJSON throws, and it answers ok:false

nodes.label: getMaintenanceList received
nodes.detail: Re-broadcasts the list to that user. The return value is just ok; the content arrives on the maintenanceList event

nodes.label: getMonitorMaintenance received
nodes.detail: Joins the link table with the monitor table and returns only the target monitor IDs. It is not narrowed by owner

nodes.label: getMaintenanceStatusPage received
nodes.detail: Joins the link table with the status page table and returns the ids and titles

nodes.label: deleteMaintenance received
nodes.detail: If it is in memory it is stopped and removed first, then the row matching id and user_id is deleted. The cache is dropped too

nodes.label: pauseMaintenance received
nodes.detail: Not in memory gives Maintenance not found. Sets active false, saves, and stops the cron

nodes.label: resumeMaintenance received
nodes.detail: Sets active true, saves and calls run(). A failure inside run is swallowed and only the success toast comes back

nodes.label: Fetch the status page
nodes.detail: The GET that returns the public page JSON. apicache holds it for 5 minutes, so an announcement takes up to five minutes to appear or disappear

nodes.label: Check login
nodes.detail: Throws You are not logged in. when socket.userID is missing. Each handler's try catches it and answers ok:false

nodes.label: Pack the form into a bean
nodes.detail: Dates are checked for validity and for a year at or below 9999. The cron strategy validates the duration and the expression; the recurring strategies build a cron from the time, weekday or day of month and validate that

nodes.label: Validate the cron expression
nodes.detail: A check that builds a Cron and immediately stops it. An invalid one throws and aborts before saving

nodes.label: Build the cron expression
nodes.detail: For a recurring strategy it builds the cron string from the start time and the weekday or day of month, and works out the duration. For month end, only lastDay1 maps to L

nodes.label: Work out the duration
nodes.detail: Takes the difference between the start and end times in seconds. A window crossing midnight gets 24 hours added to keep it positive

nodes.label: Arm the schedule
nodes.detail: Stops any existing job and rebuilds it. Old data with no cron gets one generated and saved here. The manual strategy does nothing

nodes.label: Stop the schedule
nodes.detail: Stops the cron job and drops the reference. It does not cancel a running window's end timer, so the state survives until the next broadcast

nodes.label: Work out the running window
nodes.detail: Builds a window from the next run time minus the duration and, if now is inside it, returns the start and end. Outside it, null

nodes.label: Decide this run's length
nodes.detail: Uses the remaining time if one was given, otherwise the duration. Near the end date it is trimmed to the end date

nodes.label: Work out the current status
nodes.detail: Inactive when paused, always under maintenance for the manual strategy, scheduled before the start, ended past the end date. Anything else comes from the in-memory state

nodes.label: Under maintenance?
nodes.detail: A boolean that only looks at whether the status is under-maintenance. Both the monitoring side and the status page side use it

nodes.label: Resolve the timezone
nodes.detail: Unset, or set to the same as the server, returns the server timezone. The cron fires according to it

nodes.label: Convert to screen JSON
nodes.detail: Packs in the status, the timezone and the current and next windows. The windows are computed from the cron job every time, not read from the DB

nodes.label: Broadcast the list
nodes.detail: An entry point that only pulls the user ID off the acting socket and hands it to the broadcast

nodes.label: Broadcast the list to a user
nodes.detail: Sends maintenanceList to that user's room. Every tab of the same user updates at once

nodes.label: Turn the list into JSON
nodes.detail: Converts every maintenance in memory. It is not narrowed by the user ID argument, so other users' entries are mixed in

nodes.label: Load everything at startup
nodes.detail: Puts every maintenance from the DB into memory and calls run. It is not awaited, so the state can be undecided right after startup

nodes.label: Get one from memory
nodes.detail: Reads from the in-memory list. Something present in the DB but not in memory comes back null

nodes.label: Drop the public page cache
nodes.detail: Throws away every status-page HTTP cache. Without it, the old announcement stays visible for up to five minutes

nodes.label: Is the monitor under maintenance?
nodes.detail: Looks at every linked maintenance and is true if any one is running. If a parent group is a target, its children are recursively true as well

nodes.label: Is this change worth notifying?
nodes.detail: Only maintenance to down is notified. Up to maintenance, maintenance to up and down to maintenance are all silent

nodes.label: Compose the down / recovery notification
nodes.detail: Compose the down / recovery notification

nodes.label: Send to the notification provider
nodes.detail: Dispatch to the notification provider

nodes.label: Update the uptime totals
nodes.detail: Updates the uptime totals. A beat during maintenance counts as neither up nor down; it is tallied separately as maintenance

nodes.label: Build the public page data
nodes.detail: Builds and returns the maintenance announcements array along with the settings, the incidents and the group list

nodes.label: Pick the maintenance to announce
nodes.detail: Of the windows linked to that page, only the running ones become public JSON. An exception along the way silently yields an empty array

nodes.label: Single-window start job
nodes.detail: Fires once at the start time, re-broadcasts the list and drops the public page cache. The end is left to the end-time check

nodes.label: Maintenance start
nodes.detail: Sets the status to running, clears the previous end timer, arms a new one and writes the last start time to the DB

nodes.label: End timer
nodes.detail: After the duration it puts the status back to scheduled and broadcasts the list. It is an in-process timer, so a restart loses it

nodes.label: Interval recurrence job
nodes.detail: Fires at the start time every day and only starts when enough days have passed since the last start. It counts from the start date

nodes.label: Skipped for being too soon
nodes.detail: On a day that has not reached the interval it does nothing. It allows 1.1 hours of slack to absorb clock drift

nodes.label: cron / weekday / day-of-month job
nodes.detail: Fires on the generated or entered cron expression. The timezone follows each maintenance's own setting

nodes.label: One monitoring beat
nodes.detail: The body of one monitoring beat. It checks for maintenance first and, if so, sets the status to maintenance without probing anything

nodes.label: Schedule the next beat
nodes.detail: Schedule the next beat

nodes.label: maintenance
nodes.detail: The maintenance itself: title, description, creator, active flag, strategy, start and end dates, times, weekdays, cron and duration

nodes.label: monitor_maintenance
nodes.detail: Links a maintenance to its target monitors. Cascades away when the maintenance is deleted

nodes.label: maintenance_status_page
nodes.detail: Links a maintenance to the status pages that announce it. Deleting either side cascades

nodes.label: status_page
nodes.detail: The public status pages. The source of the announcement candidates and their display names

nodes.label: monitor
nodes.detail: The monitored targets. Used for the target monitor choices and to confirm they exist

nodes.label: heartbeat
nodes.detail: One row of check results. During maintenance it records status 3 (maintenance) and Monitor under maintenance

flows.title: Schedule a maintenance
flows.trigger: "Schedule Maintenance" on the maintenance screen, then filling in the form and pressing "Save"

steps.label: The default is a single window, one hour from now
A single window shows the quick duration buttons
Fill in the end time automatically
Aborted when the start time is empty
Aborted when both targets are empty
Not logged in throws and gives ok:false
Pack the input into a bean
A malformed expression aborts before saving
Insert a row and record the creator
Arm the schedule right after creating it
Decide the recipient from the user ID

notes: Cloning takes the same path. After loading it only clears the id and adds cloneOf to the title, so saving creates a new one
The save is three round trips: the maintenance itself, the target monitors and the target status pages. If only the first succeeds, the maintenance is still there and a success toast still appears
The manual strategy builds no cron and counts as running from the moment it is created
The run right after an add is called in the mode that reports failure by throwing, but that exception is caught by addMaintenance's try and turns into ok:false

flows.title: Assign the target monitors
flows.trigger: Picking the target monitors on the edit screen and pressing "Save" (it follows the main save automatically)

steps.label: Sent after the main save succeeds
Not logged in throws and gives ok:false
A failure only toasts and it carries on

notes: It always deletes everything and re-inserts, so an empty payload clears every link. Two saves at once means last write wins
There is a login check but no owner check, so anyone who knows the ID can rewrite another user's maintenance targets
Choosing a parent group as a target makes the monitors under it count as under maintenance too, through the monitoring side's check
This step does not re-broadcast the list. The screen catches up on the refetch that follows the status page registration

flows.title: Assign the target status pages
flows.trigger: Picking the announcement pages on the edit screen (or ticking show on all pages) and pressing "Save"

steps.label: Not logged in throws and gives ok:false
Decide the recipient from the user ID
Back to the list screen, updated

notes: "Show on all status pages" only expands the candidates as they are at save time. A page created later is never announced automatically
When the edit screen is reopened, a link count equal to the candidate count is restored as "all pages"
This one also deletes everything and re-inserts, and the only ownership check is being logged in

flows.title: Load a saved maintenance into the edit screen

steps.label: Read the one row with your own ID
Someone else's ID throws and gives ok:false
Show the fields for that strategy
Look up the target monitor IDs
Look up the announcement page IDs and titles

notes: Restoring the target monitors assumes the monitor list has finished loading. An ID missing from it (a deleted monitor, say) leaves undefined in the picker
Cloning loads exactly the same way and only then clears the ID and rewrites the title
socket.js has wrappers for getMonitorMaintenance and getMaintenanceStatusPage, but the edit screen emits directly instead of using them

flows.title: Edit a saved maintenance
flows.trigger: Fixing the content on the edit screen and pressing "Save"

steps.label: Anyone but the creator gets a permission error
Check whether now is inside a window
Inside a window, start with the time remaining

notes: An edit pulls the target from the in-memory list, so an ID that is not there leaves bean null and produces a "cannot read property" style exception message
Every save stops and rebuilds the cron job, so saving during a window is treated as a restart from that moment through the inside-the-window check
The old job stops, but the end timer armed just before it does not. The status can flicker briefly right after a save
An edit re-registers both the target monitors and the announcement pages after the main save. Targets removed on screen disappear here

flows.title: A window starts
flows.trigger: The cron fires at the configured time (or a save, a resume or a restart finds itself inside the window)

steps.label: Start once the interval is met
Do nothing on a day that is too soon
A single window drops the cache at its start
On re-arming, check whether now is inside a window
Inside a window, start with the time remaining
Broadcast the list to the creator
The row takes the under-maintenance colour
Treated as under maintenance from the next beat

notes: Starting only sets the status to running in memory; the running flag never reaches the DB. A restart works it out again from the inside-the-window check
An automatic cron start does not drop the public page cache (only the single-window job does). The announcement can take up to five minutes to show
Before the start date or after the end date, the status check wins: even when the cron fires it still reads scheduled or ended
Interval recurrence fires daily and counts days. It discounts 1.1 hours from the gap since the last start to absorb clock drift
The manual strategy creates no job and counts as running the whole time it is active

flows.title: A window ends
flows.trigger: The duration's end timer fires (or the end date passes)

steps.label: Put the status back to scheduled
Work out the next window again
Past the end date it reads as ended
Back to the scheduled / ended look
Back to normal monitoring on the next beat

notes: Ending relies on an in-process timer. Across a restart it never fires; instead the inside-the-window check on re-arming squares things up
A window near the end date is trimmed to the end date, so it can finish sooner than the duration
The public page cache is not dropped at the end either, so the announcement takes up to five minutes to disappear
The monitoring side consults the links on every beat rather than a timer, so the end takes effect on the very next beat

flows.title: Pause a maintenance
flows.trigger: Pressing "Pause" in the list and answering "Yes"

steps.label: Save the active flag as false
Back to normal monitoring on the next beat

notes: Inactive wins over everything in the status check, so even a running window immediately stops counting as maintenance
The cron job stops, but the end timer armed during a running window does not. It fires after the pause and slips in one extra list broadcast
There is no owner check: anyone logged in can pause another user's maintenance
Only pause and delete go through a confirm dialog; resume runs immediately

flows.title: Resume a maintenance
flows.trigger: Pressing "Resume" in the list (no confirmation, it runs at once)

steps.label: Save the active flag as true
Generate the cron if there is none
Check whether now is inside a window
Inside a window, running straight away
The button goes back to Pause

notes: The re-arm on resume is called in the mode that does not throw on failure, so a broken cron still produces a success toast and leaves the state unknown
If the moment of resuming falls inside a window, it starts running there and then rather than waiting for the next firing
The manual strategy goes straight back to running the moment it is resumed

flows.title: Delete a maintenance
flows.trigger: Pressing "Delete" in the list and answering "Yes"

steps.label: Delete only the row with your own ID
The target monitor links go too
The announcement page links go too
Back to normal monitoring on the next beat

notes: The links are left to the database's cascade. There is no dedicated delete for them

Removal from memory happens regardless of the creator, but the DB delete only touches rows whose creator matches. Send someone else's ID and the schedule stops while the row survives, to return on the next restart
An ID that does not exist still comes back as a success
Delete one while it is running and its target monitors go back to normal checks on the next beat

flows.title: During maintenance nothing is marked down and nothing is notified

steps.label: Check for maintenance before probing anything
Not counted in the uptime, tallied separately
Entering and leaving are not notified, move on
Only maintenance to down is notified

notes: During maintenance it makes no real request: it pins the status to maintenance and records Monitor under maintenance. No response time is measured either
If a parent group is a maintenance target, its child monitors are automatically treated as under maintenance too (the check recurses up through the parents)
Up to maintenance and maintenance to up are not notified. Only turning down while under maintenance is
The check queries the DB on every beat, so a start, an end, a pause or a delete all take effect on the next beat
A push monitor goes through the same check when a beat arrives, and during maintenance its status is overwritten with maintenance

flows.title: Show the announcement on the status page
flows.trigger: A visitor opens the public status page

steps.label: Look the page up by slug
Look up the linked maintenance IDs
Convert only the running ones for the public
Put it into the JSON as an announcement
An exception silently means no announcement

notes: Only the running ones are announced. Scheduled windows never appear on the public page
This response is cached for five minutes. A settings change drops the cache, but an automatic cron start or end does not, so it can take up to five minutes to appear or disappear
The target monitors are shown by a different mechanism. A monitor under maintenance turns its status on the page into the maintenance state
An exception while fetching the maintenance list only returns an empty array; the page itself does not error (just the announcement vanishes)

flows.title: Restore the schedules on restart
flows.trigger: Server startup (right after the database is ready)

steps.label: Arm the schedules one by one
Old data gets a cron generated
The interval strategy is built from the start date
A single window fires once, at the start time
Check whether now is inside a window
Inside a window, resume with the time remaining
From here on it is included in the broadcasts
Right after startup it can read as unknown

notes: Whether a window is running is not stored in the DB. After a restart it is restored purely from the inside-the-window check, so anything but a single window or the manual strategy falls back to scheduled once it is outside its window
The startup load does not wait for each entry's schedule to be armed. Open the list before they are and the status can read unknown
The startup call passes its argument differently from the others, choosing the behaviour that throws on failure. One broken cron can halt the whole load part way
Old data with an empty cron gets one generated here and written straight back to the DB
